cause_attributed: Relationship problems, substance use, physical health problems, and job/financial problems as circumstances contributing to suicide (beyond mental health conditions)
document: Vital Signs: Trends in State Suicide Rates — United States, 1999–2016 and Circumstances Contributing to Suicide — 27 States, 2015 (MMWR)
supporting_line: Relationship, substance use, health, and job or financial problems are among the other circumstances contributing to suicide.

cause_attributed: COUNTER/COMPLICATION of mental-illness-only attribution: a majority of suicide decedents had no known mental health condition
supporting_line: Fifty-four percent of decedents in 27 states in 2015 did not have a known mental health condition; among these, relationship problems/loss, life stressors, and recent/impending crises were more common than among decedents with known conditions.

cause_attributed: Crisis moments with breakdown in ability to deal with life stresses (financial problems, relationship disputes, chronic pain/illness); conflict, disaster, violence, abuse, loss, sense of isolation; prior attempt; links to depression and alcohol use disorders
supporting_line: Many suicides happen impulsively in moments of crisis with a breakdown in the ability to deal with life stresses... experiencing conflict, disaster, violence, abuse or loss and a sense of isolation are strongly associated with suicidal behaviour.

cause_attributed: Social isolation and loneliness as predictor/contributor to suicidal ideation and behavior
document: Our Epidemic of Loneliness and Isolation (advisory)
supporting_line: Social isolation is arguably the strongest and most reliable predictor of suicidal ideation, attempts, and lethal suicidal behavior.

cause_attributed: Household firearm access as factor associated with elevated suicide risk (access factor only; no method detail)
document: The Accessibility of Firearms and Risk for Suicide and Homicide Victimization Among Household Members, Annals of Internal Medicine
supporting_line: Access to firearms is associated with risk for completed suicide and being the victim of homicide (pooled OR for suicide 3.24, 95% CI 2.41-4.40).

cause_attributed: Cumulative economic and social disadvantage among working-class whites without a college degree ('deaths of despair': suicide, drug overdose, alcoholic liver disease)
document: Mortality and Morbidity in the 21st Century, Brookings Papers on Economic Activity, Spring 2017
supporting_line: Case and Deaton document an accumulation of pain, distress, and social dysfunction in the lives of working class whites that took hold as the blue-collar economic heyday of the early 1970s ended.

cause_attributed: COUNTER-ATTRIBUTION to deaths-of-despair: the drug environment (supply, availability, cost), not deteriorating economic conditions, primarily drives the fatal-overdose component
document: Deaths of Despair or Drug Problems?, NBER WP 24188
supporting_line: Changes in economic conditions account for less than one-tenth of the rise in drug and opioid-involved mortality rates... likely to primarily reflect drug problems rather than deaths of despair.

cause_attributed: Drug overdose and suicide as drivers of declining US life expectancy (2015-2018), framed as preventable
document: CDC Director's Media Statement on U.S. Life Expectancy
supporting_line: This troubling trend is largely driven by deaths from drug overdose and suicide.

cause_attributed: Opioid overdose deaths attributed to three waves: increased opioid prescribing (1990s), heroin (2010), illicitly manufactured fentanyl (2013)
supporting_line: The first wave began with increased prescribing of opioids in the 1990s... second wave began in 2010 (heroin)... third wave began in 2013, with substantial increases in overdose deaths involving synthetic opioids, particularly illegally made fentanyl.

cause_attributed: Increased new-media screen time (smartphones/social media) after 2010 linked to rises in adolescent depressive symptoms and suicide-related outcomes
supporting_line: Adolescents who spent more time on new media were more likely to report mental health issues.
contested_by: Odgers (2024), Nature (c14); Ophir et al. (2019) methodological comment

cause_attributed: COVID-19 pandemic — social isolation, work/support constraints, loneliness, fear of infection, grief, financial worries — driving 25% global increase in anxiety and depression
supporting_line: One major explanation for the increase is the unprecedented stress caused by the social isolation resulting from the pandemic.

cause_attributed: Pre-pandemic societal stressors (climate change, income inequality, racial injustice, opioid epidemic, gun violence), self-worth-eroding media messages, irresponsibly deployed technology; pandemic exacerbation
supporting_line: Young people are bombarded with messages through the media and popular culture that erode their sense of self-worth.

cause_attributed: Heavy social media use (>3 hrs/day) as risk factor doubling adolescents' risk of depression and anxiety symptoms
document: Social Media and Youth Mental Health (advisory)
supporting_line: Adolescents who spent more than 3 hours per day on social media faced double the risk of experiencing poor mental health outcomes. (Advisory notes most research is correlational, relationship 'complex and potentially bidirectional.')

cause_attributed: COUNTER-ATTRIBUTION: social media/smartphone causation of teen mental illness rise unsupported; causes attributed instead to poverty, violence, discrimination, opioid epidemic, inadequate mental health services
document: The great rewiring: is social media really behind an epidemic of teenage mental illness?
supporting_line: The book's repeated suggestion that digital technologies are rewiring our children's brains and causing an epidemic of mental illness is not supported by science.

cause_attributed: Loneliness and social isolation as contributors to depression and anxiety across age groups
document: Our Epidemic of Loneliness and Isolation (advisory)
supporting_line: The odds of developing depression in adults is more than double among people who report feeling lonely often.

cause_attributed: For worsening parental mental health: financial strain, work-family conflict, children's health struggles, social isolation, online 'culture of comparison,' children's technology/social media use
supporting_line: Nearly 70% of parents say parenting is now more difficult than it was 20 years ago, with children's use of technology and social media as the top two cited reasons.

cause_attributed: Behavioral health workforce shortage as driver of unmet mental health need (projected 2038 shortfalls: 99,780 mental health counselors, 99,840 psychologists, 43,810 psychiatrists)
attributed_by: HRSA National Center for Health Workforce Analysis
document: Health Workforce Projections: Behavioral Health (updated Dec 2025)
supporting_line: These estimates do not address the large amount of unmet need that exists for these same services.

cause_attributed: Health-plan noncompliance with mental health parity law (stricter prior authorization, step therapy, reimbursement limits on MH/SUD benefits) as barrier restricting access
attributed_by: US Departments of Labor, HHS, Treasury
supporting_line: EBSA identified impermissible treatment limitations applied only to MH/SUD benefits, preventing individuals from accessing covered care.

cause_attributed: Pandemic-era telehealth expansion and easing of in-person visit requirement for Schedule II prescriptions as hypothesized contributors to rising stimulant fills
document: Trends in Stimulant Prescription Fills Among Commercially Insured Children and Adults — United States, 2016–2021
supporting_line: The combination of potential increased need and reduced barriers to access might have encouraged more adults with ADHD symptoms to seek diagnosis and treatment. (Authors caution increases 'cannot be directly attributed' to telehealth policies.)

cause_attributed: Diagnostic expansion/overdiagnosis: broadening of ADHD criteria and diagnosis of milder cases contributing to rising diagnosis and treatment rates in youth
supporting_line: This review found evidence of ADHD overdiagnosis and overtreatment in children and adolescents.

cause_attributed: Growth in US antidepressant use attributed to lengthening duration of treatment (long-term use >=24 months) rather than more short-term initiations
supporting_line: Long-term use rose from 3.0% to 6.9% (1999-2010) while medium- and short-term use did not change appreciably.

cause_attributed: Reductions in smoking, earlier detection, treatment advances
Diets high in red meat and salt, low fruit/milk; alcohol; tobacco; physical inactivity, excess weight, high blood sugar as contributing
Part of recorded rise may reflect registry data quality; unclear contribution of screening and early-life environmental exposure
Decreasing fertility rates and rising obesity as primary drivers; alcohol (16% of cases), inactivity (7%)
document: ACS Cancer Statistics 2026 via Docwire News

cause_attributed: Screening at 45+ ('Starting screening at age 45 works'); young-onset rise explicitly UNEXPLAINED per ACS
Social isolation, work/support constraints, loneliness, fear of infection, grief, financial worries; young people and women most affected
Naloxone distribution, better treatment access, shifts in illegal drug supply, resumed prevention post-pandemic, prevention investment
Declines in mortality from unintentional injuries (drug overdoses), COVID-19, chronic diseases
Off-label/off-licence use (autism, EUPD, challenging behaviour, dementia), shift from specialists to GPs, 'medicalisation' of psychosocial distress — NOT rising psychosis prevalence
Telehealth expansion + eased in-person requirements for Schedule II prescribing during COVID-19, plus pandemic mental-health strain (authors caution: cannot be directly attributed)
'Growing awareness, detection, and treatment of adult ADHD'
Pandemic mental-health deterioration + 6-9-month psychotherapy waitlists pushing prescribing; male adolescent decline attributed to reduced healthcare contact/school closures cutting detection
document: Chua et al., Pediatrics, 2024-02-26 (via IHPI release)

cause_attributed: Teva manufacturing delays + insufficient supply from other manufacturers vs US demand
Population growth and ageing — explicitly not rising age-standardised rates
Diagnostic transition/reclassification within the spectrum (schizotypal growth; ~3% rediagnosis), not rising incidence
